body:
Review pass 22. Epic 7 in flight (crossnobis.R written 6 seconds before I looked), so no review of that. Instead I swept for other instances of the p0 pattern, since a defect like that is rarely a single site.

bd-01KZXQAW39E8XCXJJVW7C7M2M6 has THREE sites, not one. All densify the same m-by-p sparse frame, so all cost 18.6 GiB at p = 50000:

  R/measurement.R:494               .additive_frame_signature         weights = as.matrix(frame$weights)
  R/measurement.R:511               .measurement_frame_from_additive  weights <- as.matrix(frame$weights)
  R/measurement-decomposition.R:76  frame decomposition               weights <- as.matrix(frame$weights)

.measurement_frame_from_additive triggers it twice - directly at :511 and again through .additive_frame_signature at :513.

Only the first is on the plan path that fails today. The other two are latent, sitting in the measurement-form and decomposition subsystems - which is precisely the half that is supposed to reach brain scale later. Worth routing all three through one canonicalized helper rather than patching the one that currently fires.

CHECKED AND CLEAN, no action needed - recording so nobody re-audits these:
- R/metric.R:608-621 (.frame_metric_node) handles sparse rows correctly via Matrix::summary, with as.numeric only as a genuine non-sparse fallback.
- as.matrix() in measurement-kernel.R:137/366/585, measurement-result.R:100/120/414/468/803, evidence-task.R:620/651 all act on query$operator, which is q-by-q on the experimental side. Small, fine.
- support-index.R:158/208 are expand.grid offsets, unrelated.

Your Epic 7 opening note - "removes per-edge global combined-pair vectors: providers gather and canonically combine only each requested local covariance" - is going after the same class of problem, global p-scale allocations. Worth folding the frame-hash sites into that sweep while you are in there.

Still unfixed as of this pass: the dense coercion at measurement.R:494. Corrected fix (with drop0 canonicalization) is in the decision note on the bead.
